instruction: Explain Writing Tips for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
Use the proper VA form! VA Form 21-10210 is the latest and greatest form they should use. Keep it brief and to the point, remember BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front). The rater doesn't have time to get lost in a great story about the time Pvt. Reddit put LT's patrol cap in the freezer, after filling it with water. (But the people at r/Veterans do.) Quantify (state numbers) when possible. Which sounds better?: Veteran's headaches are so severe s(he) has to lay down for most of the day. These headaches occur fairly frequently ; OR Veteran's headaches are so severe s(he) has to lay down for most of the day. These headaches occur at least three times a week . Unless your buddy is a licensed physician in the relevant area of medicine, they should NOT try to diagnosis the Veteran. Remember, have them stick to the facts of their direct observations! But if your buddy does just so happen to be a licensed physician in the relevant area of medicine . Have them complete a Disability Benefit Questionnaires (DBQs) and/or an Independent Medical Opinion (IMO)/Nexus Letter . IMPORTANT NOTES: Do NOT tell your buddy what to write!! They must write what they SAW in relation to you and your claim. So if they did not witness anything or they recall something differently.... Well that's that! Again… the buddy can ONLY write about something they have first-hand experience (they saw you get hurt, remember you having issues, seen you have current issues, etc.). They CANNOT write about something they heard or learned about second hand (even if the person they heard something from is now dead). Hearsay itself does not help prove anything. So a statement of ““X told me Buddy had been involved in a vehicle accident and was given a cast.” Provides NO value to a claim/appeal. But DO tell them how to write the letter. If your buddy for whatever reason does not want to use the VA form. Ensure that they write "I CERTIFY THAT I have completed this statement and that its information is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief." Directly above where they sign and date their letter. In addition to providing their contact information.
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Buddy Letters/Statements

instruction: Explain 7502 Nephritis for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
Swelling of the kidney. Rated under Kidney failure . PYRAMIDING NOTES: As nephritis is often connected to Heart diseases (this does include Hypertension ). If the Veteran has both and they can be determined to be caused by the same general condition. Then the Veteran will only receive a singular rating for either the nephritis or the heart disease - whichever is higher. EXCEPTIONS to receiving the singular ratings for the heart and kidneys: If the nephritis was so advanced that it required regular dialysis. Then the Veteran CAN get both ratings even if they were caused by the same general condition. Veteran only has a single kidney, EVEN IF removal was required because of nephritis. PRESUMPTIVE CONDITION: If diagnosed within a Year of separation AND the severity warranted at least a 10% evaluation within that time. RATER NOTES: Albuminuria alone is NOT nephritis. Do NOT accept the presence of transient symptoms, such as elevated albumin and the presence of casts following febrile illness as establishing nephritis.
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Rating Schedule for the Genitourinary System

instruction: Explain Liberalizing Change of Law (38 CFR 3.114) for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
A liberalizing law is one which brings about a substantive change in the law or VA policy, creating a new and different entitlement to a benefit. This usually takes the form of Congress or the VA itself adding a new Presumptive service-condition OR changes the criteria of an existing presumptive. The impact of liberalizing law on effective dates are as follows: If claim is initiated WITHIN a year of the effective date of the law change AND all criteria of the presumptive were meet ON OR BEFORE date of law change: If granted service-connection with the basis being the change in law then the effective date will the date the law changed. IE you initiated a claim on May 9, 2023 for Hypertension (that you were diagnosed with on February 1, 2022) based on your Vietnam Agent Orange (AO) exposure. As PACT ACT was passed August 10, 2022; you are entitled to an effective date of August 10, 2022. If claim is initiated AFTER a year of the effective date of the law change AND all criteria of the presumptive were meet ON OR BEFORE date of law change: If granted service-connection with the basis being the change in law then the effective date will be a YEAR BEFORE the Veteran initiates a claim! IE You served in blue water Navy during Vietnam and were diagnosed with type II diabetes 10 years after separating from the military. If the you initiated a claim for diabetes March 3, 2023. The effective date would go back up to a year before you initiated your claim (March 3, 2022). If a claim is initiated AND NOT all criteria of the presumptive were meet ON OR BEFORE date of law change: Then you CANNOT get an earlier effective date under liberalizing law. IMPORTANT NOTES: In situations where there are multiple applicable applications of liberalizing law; The VA MUST apply the oldest applicable liberalizing law - even if it is less beneficial (as you could have filed for consideration previously). IE you were exposed to AO in Vietnam and in Thailand, you could not get renewed liberalizing law considerations under your Thailand exposures based on PACT ACT - as you were already eligible under your Vietnam AO exposures. If a Veteran becomes eligible for the first time for presumptive service-connection based on an expansion of a presumptive/changing of criteria (so their service/condition now allows such a consideration) the Veteran is eligible for consideration for ALL presumptive conditions based on that exposure based on the date of law change - even if a condition based on exposure was established years prior. IE due to PACT ACT your service in Thailand made you eligible for AO presumptive. Even though Diabetes became presumptive for AO exposure on May 8, 2001 - so long as you were diagnosed with diabetes on/before August 10, 2022, you are eligible for liberalizing law considerations. Intents to file CAN be used to get an even earlier effective date under liberalizing law (just not BEFORE the change)! As the effective date can be up to a year before the VA received the intent to file. IE Intent received on December 12, 2024 and claim received February 2025. Assuming lib law conditions were meet for a PACT ACT based grant, the effective date would be December 12, 2023. Effective dates CANNOT EVER go earlier than the date of the change, if service-connection is being based on the change of law/policy! MOST changes to the Rating schedule are NOT considered to be liberalizing. Secondary conditions Inferred or filed on the SAME DAY as the lib law impacted condition CAN get the effective date of the impacted condition (assuming Date entitlement arose does not get in the way). [ M21 V.ii.4.A.1.g ]
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Effective Dates

instruction: How do I organizing records?
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
Some of ya'll got records that are measured in inches/lbs instead of by pages! While it can be great to have a ton of evidence, it does increase the possibility of the VA/examiner missing something! This holds especially true for those of us whose records are primarily chicken-scratch doctor handwriting and/or crappy quality microfiche images. If you want to help ensure the VA does NOT miss anything, go ahead and include a table of contents as the first page of your evidence - particularly if you have a beefy military/civilian medical file. If you cannot figure out how to do this, then you can separately upload a table of contents document. IMPORTANT NOTE: You do NOT need to submit full copies of your Service Treatment Records (STRs) or private medical records. You CAN just submit the pages that are relevant/support your claims.
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Filing a VA Disability Claim

instruction: Explain 5 Years - Reductions (38 CFR 3.344) for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
A Veteran's rating generally cannot be reduced based upon a single C&P exam that shows the Veteran's disability has improved. This is because CONTINUOUS improvement MUST be shown when the evaluation has been held for at least 5 continuous years. In MOST cases it will take another exam showing the condition is still improved before the Veteran WILL receive a Proposal for reduction (if the reduction reduces your Combined evaluation; otherwise the condition will be reduced without notice). Practical example to be reduced based on ONE EXAM : The condition is rated on lab results like Kidney or Lung function and the VA happens to have lab results that show improvement… whelp if you filed an increase for that condition for some reason - you should EXPECT a reduction/proposal based if the VA does another lab test because of your claim and it confirms the improvement! IMPORTANT NOTES: This protection does NOT reset after 5 years! Meaning if you had an exam showing improvement on year 6 and then another exam shows improvement at year 16, the VA CAN still come for blood! The 5 year rule does NOT protect against Clear and Unmistakable Errors . Ratings for diseases subject to temporary or episodic improvement, e.g., Manic depressive or Other psychotic reaction , Epilepsy , Psychoneurotic reaction , Arteriosclerotic heart disease , Bronchial asthma , Gastric or duodenal ulcer , many Skin diseases , etc., will NOT be reduced based off of ONE examination showing improvement ( EXCEPT when all the evidence of record clearly shows that sustained improvement has been shown). Conditions granted temporary 100% are NOT protected by this regulation! Ratings for conditions which become comparatively symptom free (findings absent) after prolonged rest, e.g. residuals of Phlebitis , arteriosclerotic heart disease, etc., will NOT be reduced on examinations reflecting the improvement is due to bed rest . RATER COMMENT : Yeah… so… if you did not claim an increase for something unrelated to your claim and there is evidence of improvement - We ain’t gonna go out of our ways to reduce you for that unclaimed/unrelated condition.
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - The Rating Schedule Index

instruction: Explain Applying for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
SMC is something that is generally automatically awarded and is not something you need to file for, when the VA has evidence you meet the requirement(s). However, SMC K, Aid and Attendance SMC L, SMC R, SMC T, and Housebound (factually) are things you generally do need to file for so VA can get the evidence required to support a grant. SMC K has no special forms or processes, simply file it as you would any VA claim . For information on how to apply for Aid and Attendance and Housebound click HERE . Applying for SMC is NOT automatically considered to be a claim for increase; HOWEVER, the VA CAN treat it as such!
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Special Monthly Compensation (SMC)

instruction: Explain Adding Dependents for VA disability claims
output:
⚠️ COMMUNITY GUIDANCE (Not Official VA Regulations):
There are a few situations that come into play when it comes to adding dependents: Marriage Birth of a child Gaining a dependent parent Obtaining a Combined rating of at least 30% If you claim your new spouse, child, or dependent parent within 1 year of gaining them as a dependent your effective date can go back up to a year. If you are past that year then the effective date will be the date you initiate the dependent claim. If you have just received a combined rating of at least 30% then the effective date of your added dependent(s) will be identical to that of your disability claim or the date of your marriage, birth of child, or gaining a dependent parent - whichever is later.
Source: Veterans Benefits Knowledge Base - Effective Dates
